items.title: Finite Gaussian-process regression observation model
items.statement: Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, let $m:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$, and let $k:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ be symmetric and positive semidefinite, meaning that for every finite ordered list $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ in $\mathcal X$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^r$, $$\sum_{i,j=1}^r a_i a_j k(t_i,t_j)\ge0.$$ For finite ordered lists $A=(a_i)_{i=1}^r$ and $B=(b_j)_{j=1}^s$ in $\mathcal X$, define $$K_{AB}=(k(a_i,b_j))_{i,j};$$ repeated indices are allowed. Given a real Gaussian process $f=(f_t)_{t\in\mathcal X}$ with mean $m(t)=\mathbb E[f_t]$ and covariance $k(s,t)=\mathbb E[(f_s-m(s))(f_t-m(t))]$, and a nonempty finite training list $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ in $\mathcal X$, define $f_X=(f_{x_i})_{i=1}^n$ and $m_X=(m(x_i))_{i=1}^n$. For an independent centered Gaussian noise vector $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,R)$ with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance $R$, define the observation vector $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$ and the matrix $A_X=K_{XX}+R$. For a nonempty finite test list $X_*=(x_j^*)_{j=1}^p$ in $\mathcal X$, define the latent test vector $f_*=f_{X_*}$. If a centered Gaussian vector $\eta_*\sim N_p(0,R_*)$ with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance $R_*$ is independent of both $f$ and $\varepsilon$, define the noisy test vector $Y_*=f_*+\eta_*$.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 §2.2
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2

items.title: Projection onto a finite-dimensional subspace of an inner-product space
items.statement: Let $H$ be a real inner-product space and $V\subseteq H$ a finite-dimensional subspace. For each $f\in H$ there is a unique $p\in V$ such that $f-p$ is orthogonal to $V$, meaning $\langle f-p,v\rangle=0$ for every $v\in V$. For every $v\in V$, $$\|f-v\|^2=\|f-p\|^2+\|p-v\|^2.$$ In particular, $\|f\|^2=\|p\|^2+\|f-p\|^2$.

references.title: Sergei Treil, Linear Algebra Done Wrong, Chapter 5 §5.3.2

items.title: Positive definiteness is exactly the inverse condition for the observed GP covariance
items.statement: In the finite observation model, let $K=K_{XX}$ and let $R$ be symmetric and positive semidefinite. Then $A=K+R$ is symmetric and positive semidefinite. Its ordinary inverse exists if and only if $A$ is positive definite, equivalently if and only if all singular values of $A$ are positive. Thus the standard inverse formulas are defined exactly under $A\succ0$; no ordinary inverse formula applies when $A$ is singular.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4 §4.1
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2

items.title: Log marginal likelihood for a finite Gaussian-process regression model
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, let $f=(f_t)_{t\in\mathcal X}$ be a real Gaussian process with mean $m$ and symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance kernel $k$, and let $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathcal X^n$ with $n\ge1$. For independent observation noise $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,R)$ with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance $R$, set $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$, $m_X=(m(x_i))$, $K_{XX}=(k(x_i,x_j))$, and $A_X=K_{XX}+R$. Suppose $A_X$ is positive definite. Define the log marginal likelihood at $y\in\mathbb R^n$ as the logarithm of the Lebesgue density of $Y$ at $y$ under this prior-predictive model. Then $Y\sim N_n(m_X,A_X)$ and $$\log p(y\mid X,m,k,R)=-\frac12(y-m_X)^TA_X^{-1}(y-m_X)-\frac12\log\det(A_X)-\frac n2\log(2\pi).$$ This formula is asserted only for the nonsingular observed-covariance case $A_X\succ0$.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 §§2.2–2.3
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2

items.title: Finite Gaussian-process regression posterior and predictive law
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, $m:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$, and $k:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ a symmetric kernel whose every finite Gram quadratic form on points of $\mathcal X$ is nonnegative. Let $f=(f_t)_{t\in\mathcal X}$ be the canonical Gaussian process with $m(t)=\mathbb E[f_t]$ and $k(s,t)=\mathbb E[(f_s-m(s))(f_t-m(t))]$. For finite ordered lists $A=(a_i)_{i=1}^r$ and $B=(b_j)_{j=1}^s$ in $\mathcal X$, set $K_{AB}=(k(a_i,b_j))$; repetitions are allowed. Take $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathcal X^n$ and $X_*=(x_j^*)_{j=1}^p\in\mathcal X^p$ with $n,p\ge1$, and write $m_X=(m(x_i))$, $m_*=(m(x_j^*))$, $f_X=(f_{x_i})$, and $f_*=(f_{x_j^*})$. Let $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,R)$ be independent of $f$, where $R$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and set $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$ and $A_X=K_{XX}+R$. Suppose $A_X$ is positive definite. Then for every $y\in\mathbb R^n$ the conditional law of $f_*$ given $Y=y$ has mean $$m_*+K_{*X}A_X^{-1}(y-m_X)$$ and covariance $$K_{**}-K_{*X}A_X^{-1}K_{X*}.$$ This covariance is positive semidefinite and may be singular. If $\eta_*\sim N_p(0,R_*)$ is independent of both $f$ and $\varepsilon$, where $R_*$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, then the conditional law of $f_*+\eta_*$ has the same mean and covariance with $R_*$ added. The displayed kernel is defined for every $y$, although regular conditional versions are determined only $P_Y$-almost surely.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 §2.2
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2

items.title: Computational costs and limits of finite Gaussian-process regression
items.statement: A real Gaussian process is a family whose finite evaluation vectors are multivariate normal. Let $T$ be a set and let $f=(f_t)_{t\in T}$ be a real Gaussian process with mean $m(t)=\mathbb E f_t$ and symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance kernel $k(s,t)=\mathbb E[(f_s-m(s))(f_t-m(t))]$; positive semidefinite means every finite Gram quadratic form is nonnegative. For $n\ge1$ and a finite training list $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ in $T$, set $f_X=(f_{x_i})$, $K_{XX}=(k(x_i,x_j))$, and let $\varepsilon$ be centered Gaussian observation noise independent of $f$, with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance $R$. Set $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$ and $A_X=K_{XX}+R\succ0$. Write the dense Cholesky factorization as $A_X=LL^T$, where $L$ is lower triangular with positive diagonal. In the scalar-operation model, where each addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, or square root counts as one operation, factorization costs $n^3/3+O(n^2)$ operations. For a test input $x_*\in T$, define $k_{x_*X}=(k(x_*,x_i))_{i=1}^n$ and $k_{Xx_*}=k_{x_*X}^T$. After factorization, the latent predictive variance $k(x_*,x_*)-k_{x_*X}A_X^{-1}k_{Xx_*}$ requires $O(n^2)$ operations, where $O(n^2)$ denotes an asymptotic operation count as $n$ grows. These are arithmetic counts, not accuracy guarantees. For an invertible real $n\times n$ matrix $A$, define its spectral condition number by $\kappa_2(A)=\lVert A\rVert_2\lVert A^{-1}\rVert_2$, where $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sup_{\lVert x\rVert_2=1}\lVert Ax\rVert_2$ for $x\in\mathbb R^n$. For $0<\epsilon<1$, $A_\epsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\epsilon)$ has condition number $1/\epsilon$, while $E=\operatorname{diag}(0,-\epsilon)$ has relative spectral-norm size $\lVert E\rVert_2/\lVert A_\epsilon\rVert_2=\epsilon$ even though $A_\epsilon+E$ is singular. The negative log marginal likelihood need not be convex in a covariance hyperparameter. On the one-point set $T=\{t\}$, take the centered Gaussian prior $f_t\sim N(0,\theta)$ with $\theta\ge0$, covariance kernel $k_\theta(t,t)=\theta$, and independent observation noise $\varepsilon\sim N(0,1)$. For observation $Y=f_t+\varepsilon$ at $y=0$, the observed covariance is $A_\theta=1+\theta>0$ and the negative log marginal likelihood is $$L(\theta)=\tfrac12\log(1+\theta)+\tfrac12\log(2\pi).$$ For every $\theta>0$, its second derivative is $L''(\theta)=-1/(2(1+\theta)^2)<0$, so $L$ is not convex on its parameter domain. The finite Gaussian-process regression posterior formula uses Gaussian observation noise. Write $\phi(z)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/2}$ for the standard normal density and $\Phi(z)=\int_{-\infty}^z\phi(t)\,dt$ for its cumulative distribution function. With one latent value $z\sim N(0,1)$ and one positive label, the logistic likelihood $P(y=1\mid z)=\sigma(z)=(1+e^{-z})^{-1}$ or probit likelihood $P(y=1\mid z)=\Phi(z)$ gives a non-Gaussian posterior: the posterior log density has nonzero third derivative at $z=\log 3$ for logistic and $z=0$ for probit. Both likelihoods lie in $(0,1)$, so multiplying by the standard normal density gives a finite, positive normalizing integral. Finally, a Gaussian process specifies finite-dimensional laws but need not have continuous paths. A continuous modification means a process on the same probability space that agrees almost surely at each fixed input and has almost surely continuous sample paths. Under AC, on $T=[0,1]$ the equality kernel $k(s,t)=1$ when $s=t$ and $0$ otherwise has no continuous modification.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 §§2.2–2.3
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 3 §§3.3–3.4.1
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4 §4.1
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §§2.5, 2.9
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §2.9.3

items.title: Kernel ridge regression equals the Gaussian-process posterior mean
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $T$ be a set, let $k:T\times T\to\mathbb R$ be a symmetric kernel whose every finite Gram quadratic form is nonnegative, and let $m:T\to\mathbb R$. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space of functions on $T$ such that, for every $x\in T$, the section $k_x:T\to\mathbb R$, $k_x(t)=k(t,x)$, belongs to $H$ and satisfies $h(x)=\langle h,k_x\rangle_H$ for every $h\in H$. Assume $m\in H$. For a nonempty finite ordered list $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ (repetitions allowed), let $K=K_{XX}=(k(x_i,x_j))$, $m_X=(m(x_i))$, and take $y\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\sigma>0$. On the affine space $m+H$, define $$J(g)=\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-g(x_i))^2+\sigma^2\lVert g-m\rVert_H^2.$$ Then $J$ has a unique minimizer $$g_*=m+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i k_{x_i},\qquad \alpha=(K+\sigma^2 I_n)^{-1}(y-m_X).$$ Its evaluation vector is $$ (g_*(x_i))_{i=1}^n=m_X+K(K+\sigma^2I_n)^{-1}(y-m_X). $$ Under AC, the mean and kernel determine a canonical cylinder-space Gaussian-process prior. If it is observed at $X$ with independent $N_n(0,\sigma^2I_n)$ noise, this vector is the conditional mean of the latent evaluation vector given the observation $Y=y$. The Hilbert-space existence and reproducing-section properties are hypotheses here; the theorem makes no general kernel-to-Hilbert-space existence claim.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.4
Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, and Jerome Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., §5.8
Sergei Treil, Linear Algebra Done Wrong, Chapter 5 §§5.3.2, 5.4.1

items.title: Noisy interpolation on two independent coordinates
items.statement: Assume AC and take $T=\{a,b\}$ with distinct points, mean $m=0$, and equality kernel $k(s,t)=1$ if $s=t$ and $0$ otherwise. Use the canonical cylinder-space Gaussian-process prior with this mean and kernel. For $X=(a,b)$, set $K_{XX}=(k(x_i,x_j))=I_2$; observe with covariance $R=I_2$, so $A_X=K_{XX}+R=2I_2$, and data $y=(2,-1)^T$. Predict at $X_*=X$. The latent posterior mean is $(1,-\tfrac12)^T$ and its covariance is $\tfrac12 I_2$. If an independent future observation-noise vector with covariance $R_*=I_2$ is added, the noisy predictive mean is unchanged and its covariance is $\tfrac32 I_2$.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 §2.2
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2

items.title: Positive observation noise with a singular rank-one prediction
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $T=\{a,b\}$ with distinct points, $\phi(a)=1$, $\phi(b)=2$, $m=0$, and $k(s,t)=\phi(s)\phi(t)$. Use the canonical cylinder-space Gaussian-process prior with this mean and kernel. For $X=X_*=(a,b)$, set $v=(1,2)^T$, $K_{XX}=K_{**}=vv^T$, and $R=I_2$, so $A_X=K_{XX}+R=I_2+vv^T\succ0$. With data $y=(1,0)^T$, the latent posterior mean is $v/6$ and the latent posterior covariance is $K_{XX}/6$, which is singular.

references.title: Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 §2.2
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §6.4.2
